problem:
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[4]{\pi }}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{\sqrt{\pi }}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x=$

*Hint: Change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$*
worked_solution:
We cannot integrate the given integral because we cannot find a simple antiderivative of the integrand. So, we change the order of integration.

We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,y),$ ${u}_{2}(x,y),$ ${v}_{1}(x),$ ${v}_{2}(x),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[4]{\pi }}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{\sqrt{\pi }}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt[4]{\pi },\,\,{z}^{2}\le y\le \sqrt{\pi }}
$$

Now, let's sketch the region. Since it is a type III region, we first sketch the projection onto the $xz$-plane, given by

$$
E={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt[4]{\pi }}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/3bb477b93fb92174307bee87130d9957b135cdafaa4167f78f3d603c4192391d.png)

Then, the region $R$ is shown in the diagram below, where ${z}^{2}\le y\le \sqrt{\pi }.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/cf966e9ec5fbcf11727d46bb3906f05e4b30df4c9bef86a6eab4850b967d7ba0.png)

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $R$ as a type I region and its projection $D$ onto the $xy$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $z$-axis and in the direction of increasing $z,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/88b5e19c3e263d160db8d041fd3504b25d4a8a8f7ae8e111cdeb5b153c3cd21f.png)

The arrow enters the region through the bottom boundary and leaves through the top boundary:

- The top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x,y),$ is

$$
y={z}^{2}\,⟺\,z=\sqrt{y}.
$$

- The bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=0.
$$

Therefore, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/b748578888fdda878b0d44bb036310644c3437c1922aafd49cab6c165a9cf132.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $xy$-plane with the top curve given by $y=\sqrt{\pi }.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/60e35d0e77314aaecc60b0eda3c039afa0bdd44d49f68ad39e27c8856a9390e0.png)

Hence,

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{\pi }}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[4]{\pi }}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{\sqrt{\pi }}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi }}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}z\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi }}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi }}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2}){[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi }}\frac{y}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi }}\frac{y}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}+{y}^{2})]}_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi }}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}))\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{x}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
